issues.legal_issue: A civil court may grant interim relief while an objection to its jurisdiction remains undecided, and should determine that objection at the earliest possible time.
material_facts: An injunction application and an objection to the civil court’s jurisdiction were pending in the same suit.
The civil court ruled on the objection and continued the injunction; the jurisdiction question was ultimately resolved against the court’s jurisdiction only after further proceedings.
issues.conclusion: A jurisdiction objection does not immediately disable a civil court from granting appropriate interim relief. The court should determine the jurisdiction issue at the earliest possible time, and interim orders remain effective while that issue is pending.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9-A of the Code of Civil Procedure as amended in Maharashtra makes explicit that a court may grant necessary interim relief pending determination of a jurisdiction objection, while requiring the objection to be decided as a preliminary issue as expeditiously as possible. The Court treated this as a statement of the general principle that a court is not rendered powerless merely because jurisdiction is challenged.

predicates.civil_suit_with_interim_relief: A party brought a civil suit and sought interim relief in it.
predicates.jurisdiction_objection_pending: A party objected to the court’s jurisdiction and that objection had not yet been determined.

issues.definition: When interim relief is sought in a civil suit and a jurisdiction objection remains undecided, the court may grant interim relief while that objection is pending.

issues.legal_issue: A party may be punished for disobeying an interim injunction before a court’s lack of jurisdiction is determined, even if that lack of jurisdiction is later established.
material_facts: The landlord filed the suit bona fide, believing the civil court had jurisdiction.
The civil court issued an interim injunction restraining construction, and the defendants challenged the court’s jurisdiction while the injunction remained in force.
The civil court and the High Court found that construction was carried out in breach of the injunction before the jurisdiction issue was finally decided.

The High Court later held that the civil court lacked jurisdiction to entertain the suit, and the appellate court set aside the punishment solely on the ground that the interim orders were therefore non-est.
issues.conclusion: The later finding that the civil court lacked jurisdiction did not prevent punishment for disobedience committed before that finding. The Court set aside the High Court’s decision and affirmed the order finding the second defendant guilty and sentencing him to imprisonment.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 39 Rule 2-A of the Code of Civil Procedure and Section 9-A as amended in Maharashtra, interim orders made while a jurisdiction objection is pending are orders within the court’s jurisdiction when made and must be obeyed while in force. Their later termination upon a finding of no jurisdiction does not erase liability for earlier violations. The Court relied on Shiv Chander Kapoor v. Amar Bose, State of Punjab v. Gurdev Singh, Ravi S. Naik v. Union of India, Hadkinson v. Hadkinson, United States of America v. John F. Shipp, State of U.P. v. Ratan Shukla, and Nalla Senapati Sarkarai Mandariar Pallayakottai v. Shri Ambal Mills Pvt. Ltd. It held Dwarkadas Mulji v. Shadilal Laxmidas wrongly decided and Vivekanand Atmaram Chitale v. Vidyavardhini Sabha inapplicable to civil-court orders.

rule.if: appeal_against_punishment_for_injunction_breach and civil_suit_filed_bona_fide and interim_injunction_in_force and jurisdiction_objection_later_upheld and breach_before_jurisdiction_decision

predicates.appeal_against_punishment_for_injunction: A party appealed an order punishing it for breaching an interim injunction.
predicates.civil_suit_filed_bona_fide: The plaintiff brought the civil suit in good faith, believing the court had jurisdiction.
predicates.interim_injunction_in_force: The court had issued an interim injunction that had not been set aside or stayed when the conduct occurred.
predicates.jurisdiction_objection_later_upheld: A court later determined that the civil court lacked jurisdiction to entertain the suit.
predicates.breach_before_jurisdiction_decision: The party disobeyed the injunction before the jurisdiction question was decided.

issues.definition: When a party appeals punishment for breaching an injunction in a bona fide civil suit, and the injunction was in force when breached before a later decision upholding a jurisdiction objection, the earlier breach remains punishable.

issues.legal_issue: A supported finding of wilful breach of an injunction need not be remitted for reconsideration when the appellate record provides no basis to disturb the lower courts’ consistent factual findings.
material_facts: The civil court found from photographs and other material that extensive construction had been carried out after the injunction and rejected the claim that other tenants were responsible.
The High Court later relied on reports and other records indicating continued construction and obstruction of a court-appointed commissioner.
The High Court’s decision under appeal addressed the jurisdiction question rather than the factual challenge, and the Supreme Court found no basis to remit the breach question for reconsideration.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to remit the factual issue and affirmed the civil court’s finding that the second defendant had violated the injunction.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Order 39 Rule 2-A of the Code of Civil Procedure, the Court relied on the civil court’s detailed findings and the consistent supporting findings and reports recorded in the High Court proceedings. In the absence of an indication that the factual issue had been pursued before the High Court or a basis to displace those findings, remittal would be an unnecessary formality.

rule.if: appeal_against_injunction_breach_finding and detailed_trial_finding_of_breach and consistent_supporting_record and no_basis_for_remand

predicates.appeal_against_injunction_breach_finding: A party appealed an order finding it responsible for breaching an injunction.
predicates.detailed_trial_finding_of_breach: The trial court made a reasoned finding that the party breached the injunction.
predicates.consistent_supporting_record: Other court findings or records supported the trial court’s conclusion that the party breached the injunction.
predicates.no_basis_for_remand: The appellate record showed no sufficient basis to remit the factual question for reconsideration.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an injunction-breach finding, the trial court’s detailed finding is supported by a consistent record, and there is no sufficient basis for remand, the finding is upheld without remitting the issue.
